HydrAIDE has powered Trendizz.com since 2024 — indexing millions of European websites and serving keyword search from a single server. Concrete numbers: 100K inserts in ~46 ms, 10K updates in ~3.75 ms, ~15.4 bytes per entry on disk on a Threadripper + NVMe. See benchmarks.

In 2021 we were indexing 2M+ European websites for Trendizz. Every word was stored in its own shard, and every shard listed the domains where the word appears — tens of millions of independent storage units, multiple terabytes on disk, on a single server with 128 GB of RAM and a sub-3-second search budget across the entire corpus. PostgreSQL deadlocked under the concurrent writes and slowed past tens of millions of rows. MongoDB and any RAM-resident engine wanted the working set in memory. Cloud and per-CPU-licensed engines were ruled out on cost. Disk B-trees were too slow for the latency target.

Bemi plugs into Ruby on Rails with Active Record and your existing PostgreSQL database to track data changes automatically. It unlocks robust context-aware audit trails and time travel querying inside your application.
See an example repo for a Ruby on Rails app that automatically tracks all changes.
Check out our docs for more details.

Bemi is designed to be lightweight and secure. It takes a practical approach to achieving the benefits of event sourcing without requiring rearchitecting existing code, switching to highly specialized databases, or using unnecessary git-like abstractions on top of databases. We want your system to work the way it already does with your existing database to allow keeping things as simple as possible.
On the database level, Bemi securely connects to PostgreSQL's Write-Ahead Log and implements Change Data Capture. This allows tracking even the changes that get triggered via direct SQL.

The cloud solution includes worker ingesters, queues for fault tolerance, and an automatically scalable cloud-hosted PostgreSQL. Bemi currently doesn't support a self hosted option, but contact us if this is required.

Libro is a Spring Boot REST API for the library of Aklan State University – College of Computer Studies (ASU-CCS). It manages physical book copies, user accounts, and loan history. Each catalog record is one physical copy, which keeps loan history accurate per copy (see Domain Decisions).

- **Security:** stateless HS256 JWT Bearer authentication, BCrypt passwords, per-IP rate limits on login and signup, and a uniform JSON error contract. See the JWT Authentication Design.

The single-module codebase groups `auth`, `book`, `loan`, `user`, `audit`, and `info` by feature, then by layer. Controllers accept and return DTOs; services own business rules, transactions, and entity-to-DTO mapping; repositories own persistence. Shared responses, errors, request IDs, time handling, and OpenAPI configuration live in `global`. Flyway owns the schema, and Hibernate validates it at startup. |Standardized feature packages and moved DTO mapping into services|Controllers stay focused on HTTP, and JPA entities do not cross the API boundary.|
|Moved account ownership and target-role rules into `UserAccessPolicy`|One policy handles student, faculty, assistant, and librarian account operations.|
|Introduced shared not-found and invalid-request exception types|Expected client errors have consistent status codes; unexpected faults get a generic 500 response.|
|Layered the test profile over runtime configuration|Tests exercise the real application defaults with only test-specific overrides.|
|Entity types and database columns disagreed at startup|Made Flyway the sole schema authority, aligned migrations with JPA, and kept Hibernate schema validation enabled.|
|Container startup could race PostgreSQL readiness|Added a database health check and made the app wait for a healthy database.|
|Concurrent checkout could assign one copy twice|Added row locking, a database unique index for active loans, and PostgreSQL concurrency tests.|
|HTTP-only or mocked tests could miss real persistence errors|Split fast unit/MVC tests from Testcontainers integration tests that exercise migrations, JPA, constraints, and loan races.|
|Scattered account rules and error handling were hard to audit|Centralized target-role/ownership checks in `UserAccessPolicy` and mapped client failures through shared exception types.|
